correctness.rationale: For fixed r and a, the proof reconstructs global supervenience as pairwise equality of complete predicate extensions. Mixed factorial moments: disjoint labelled pairs give (m)_(2K)/(2^K q^(aK)) -> (c²/2)^K; any connected component of ≥3 world vertices is o(1) by spanning-tree q^(-a(v-1)), and repeated differently marked edges on one pair cost an extra q^-1. Markov excludes all collisions on >a predicates; a pairwise-independence variance calculation excludes every nontrivial implication from <a predicates. The proof handles all A,B simultaneously and proves the limiting count of size-a minimal determining families. Exhaustive finite tests exercise the mapping and moment identities but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural structural question in finite-world supervenience is which families of predicate extensions determine all others, and how these dependencies co-occur. The theorem gives a complete nondegenerate law for that entire logical dependence matrix at each natural birthday threshold, including independently varying critical families and a binomial minimal-key count. This goes beyond known one-implication marginal estimates and supplies an interpretable random-model phase diagram.
